tweets.text:
Something I notice: adrenaline, dopamine, and fatigue stack up during a great win streak. It’s incredibly hard to stop trading, and as the fatigue builds, I’m tempted to size up tremendously. Part of me is relieved when the big loss finally hits, because it warrants a break.

The issue is that in most instances, like last week, if I had never sized up, I most likely wouldn’t have lost much, if anything. Smaller sizing preserves control. In that particular case, I was FORCED to close my positions so my remaining margin wouldn’t get wiped. At a quarter or a fifth of the size (my usual), I wouldn’t have had to do that, and might even have had the luxury of adding to positions (hard to say). OR I might’ve cut the trades way earlier, because on monster sizing, cutting is a difficult choice to make, and it makes a trader lose nimbleness. Getting out of a trade becomes a massive chore and a costly one, and the hopium kicks in.

Psychologically, it is painful to lose large amounts of money fast, but it’s also a relief. It’s a sort of desirable outcome, because once that happens, I know for a fact that I’ve lost control, and it’s the perfect time and justification to step away from the market.

That’s what I’m about to do: completely close the trading interfaces and not care one bit about what BTC or ETH do until October 31 (perhaps with some super wide alerts in case of extreme volatility).

I am writing this for the handful who will relate and understand, because it’s not obvious, even with introspection. It’s there, it’s a real psychological issue, and it’s avoidable with awareness.
